newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO negotiator expects Hebron deal Monday night.
newsitem.headline: PLO negotiator expects Hebron deal Monday night.

text.p: A senior PLO negotiator said he expected a deal on Hebron to be clinched later on Monday.
"We expect a deal tonight. Negotiations are continuing," said Jamil Tarifi while entering talks between PLO and Israeli officials. He did not elaborate.
Tarifi said a meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to seal an accord on the West Bank town was possible on Monday.

"A meeting between Netanyahu and Arafat is possible tonight, but we don't know yet," Tarifi said. He said it would depend on progress in talks between Palestinian and Israeli teams meeting on Monday evening.
Earlier negotiators from both sides said progress had been made in the U.S.-brokered talks to break a deadlock over Hebron by Christmas.

U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross shuttled between Israel, PLO-ruled Gaza and Egypt since his arrival in the region on Saturday to try to clinch a deal on the long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron.
